body: In India, the Minervini/Weinstein framework is widely replicated on Chartink, Screener.in, MarketInOut, Sharpely and MarketSmith India; the most rule-based, investable implementation is the NSE Nifty200 Momentum 30 index (volatility-adjusted 6- and 12-month returns, semi-annual rebalance) and its ETFs/index funds. Indian traders have featured in the US Investing Championship (USIC), but India-specific competition data is thin.

title: README › Schedule: cron

body:
- **Check dates.** Before `check_from`, no network is used for a call. India Q3 FY27 results are checked from
  10-Jan-2027 and FY27 from 15-Apr-2027. US checks start around each company's report date. Price calls are
  checked from 2-Jul-2027.
- **Exact periods.** An India number is used only when the NSE XBRL has a context with *exactly* the quarter
  or fiscal-year dates, or when screener has that column. For a US fiscal year, the 10-K for that year must
  be filed, and Q4 = FY − 9-month YTD (or a tagged 3-month Q4).
- **Two sources for India.** NSE XBRL and screener must land on the same side of the threshold. If the
  value is within `guard` of the threshold and the two sources differ by more than 0.3 pp (or 1%), or the
  rule says the company's own figure governs, the call goes to review. A single source is used only on or
  after `resolve_by`, and only when it is further than `guard` from the threshold.
- **Prices.** The resolver uses the last close on or before the end date. It reads that close only after
  the end date has passed and a later bar exists (or 4 days have gone by), and only if the close is within
  6 days of the end date. If the Yahoo start close differs from the rule's base price by more than 0.5% and
  there was no split, the call goes to review. Yahoo `close` is split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted, which
  matches the rules.
- **Events.** YES comes only from a structured signal: an 8-K Item 1.03, or a Yahoo dividend of at least the
  required amount with an ex-date on or before the deadline. A NO is always a proposal for a human to confirm.
- **Overdue.** If `resolve_by` passes with no data, the call goes to review marked OVERDUE (decide, or void
  if the source stopped publishing). It is never auto-voided.
- **Skips.** Calls already in a resolution seed are skipped, and calls whose memdb status is not `open` are
  skipped.

title: SONACOMS › 1. Method

body:
```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y python3 poppler-utils sqlite3 git curl
sudo timedatectl set-timezone Asia/Kolkata      # so cron times below are IST
git clone https://github.com/aditya-bad/fein.git ~/fein   # private repo: use a GitHub token or deploy key,
                                                          # or copy tools/detectors/ onto the Pi (plus
                                                          # tools/promise_tracker/pipeline/ for solvency_screen.py)
mkdir -p ~/fein-data
echo 'export FEIN_DATA=$HOME/fein-data' >> ~/.bashrc
```

`poppler-utils` (`pdftotext`) is not needed by the detectors; it is there for reading the filing
PDFs that alerts link to. `curl` is preinstalled on Raspberry Pi OS; BSE only answers over HTTP/2,
which Python's urllib cannot do, so `collect.py` calls `curl --http2` for BSE.

Check that everything works, then build a first baseline:

```bash
cd ~/fein/tools/detectors
python3 collect.py --selftest      # live, tiny fetch of every source, writes nothing
python3 detect.py --selftest       # live Indo Tech pledge check + offline rule tests
python3 collect.py                 # yesterday -> today
python3 detect.py
```

The pledge rules compare two snapshots, so they only start firing from the second evening.

Useful options:

```bash
python3 collect.py --from 2026-11-18 --to 2026-11-20   # backfill a range
python3 collect.py --only pledges,deals                # subset: announcements,bse,insider,sast,deals,pledges
python3 collect.py --no-bse                            # skip the BSE backup feed
python3 detect.py --from 2026-11-18 --to 2026-11-20 --all   # re-list alerts already seen
```

Exit codes: `collect.py` returns 1 only if every step failed (each step is logged and recorded in
the `runs` table); `detect.py` returns 0 unless it crashes. Only one copy of `collect.py` runs at a
time (lock file in `logs/`).

body:
1. **Keep the PEAD avoid gate as it is** (bottom-two SUE = WAIT for ≥ 63 trading days). The red flag does not make
   the 13-week drift worse, so there is no "EXIT" escalation.
2. **Add a survival cap:** bottom-two SUE **and** a red flag (pledge > 25% or interest cover < 1.5x) → no new money /
   minimum size, and a deep-dive question on the balance sheet. About 1 in 6 such events halved within a year
   (1 in 4 with pledge > 50%), against 1 in 16 for clean firms with no miss.
3. **The honest refinement:** C shows the same halving risk without a miss. So the stage-2 red flag is the tail-risk
   signal on its own (≈ 2.5× base), and the miss adds little to it. The pre-registered rule ties the cap to the
   combination. The data say the cap could apply to any red-flag firm. **That broader rule was not pre-registered, so it is a
   proposal for a future test, not an adopted rule.** S5-India should not trigger the cap (no signal here).
